artifacts.summary: Verified all 8 file_scope contract sites at current line numbers (no drift); documented lake-build-guard.sh mechanics (project-granular locking, 600s default lock-wait timeout, dead-end record on LEAN_NUM_THREADS/-j); recommended anchor content/length, guard --timeout value, scoped-build mandate extension, skill-lake-repair carve-out (guard-routed but still synchronous), twin-file MUST NOT addition, and flagged the out-of-scope lean_build MCP tool gap.

memory_candidates.content: lake-build-guard.sh (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/) locks at whole-project granularity, not per-module: `lake-build-guard.sh build -- ModuleName` still acquires the project-root flock. A contract mandating the guard for scoped phase-end builds therefore serializes normally-independent scoped builds across concurrent sessions on the same package -- a real tradeoff, not a transparent win. Its default `--timeout` (lock-wait, not build duration) is 600s, i.e. the same as the old foreground Bash cap being replaced -- a caller expecting builds that can legitimately exceed 10 minutes should pass an explicit larger --timeout or a second waiting session can itself time out (exit 75).

Bash tool command-substitution call sites ($(cmd 2>&1)) are structurally incompatible with run_in_background (which returns no stdout to a shell variable) but ARE compatible with routing through a synchronous flock-based guard wrapper, since the guard still returns stdout/exit status through $(...) unchanged. When a contract mandates both detachment and guard-routing together, a command-substitution call site can adopt the guard unchanged while being explicitly carved out of the detachment half of the mandate.
